p.src: Overview: Two small dimensionless numbers organize the evening. The first is the surviving matter–antimatter excess, rounded in the course to one part in $10^8$. Its dynamical explanation requires baryon-number violation, particle–antiparticle asymmetry, and departure from thermal equilibrium: the three Sakharov conditions. The second is the primordial density contrast, of order $10^{-5}$ at decoupling. Gravity amplifies rather than erases such ripples, so their smallness motivates inflation. We then prepare the mechanics of inflation by deriving the equation of motion of a homogeneous scalar field in an expanding universe and identifying $3H\dot\phi$ as Hubble friction.

That observation already suggests turning the question around: why did annihilation leave any unmatched matter at all?

\qquad
T:\ \psi(\mathbf x,t)\longmapsto\psi^*(\mathbf x,-t).$ Changing $t\to-t$ reverses the time derivative; complex conjugation also sends $i\to-i$, restoring the equation. For particles with spin, the antiunitary time-reversal operator carries additional structure, but the complex conjugation is already visible in this elementary case.

The present stability of the proton is compatible with this condition. In grand-unified reasoning, baryon violation can be mediated by a very heavy particle of mass $M_X$. At energies far below $M_X$, the effective amplitude is suppressed schematically by inverse powers, $\begin{aligned}
\mathcal A_{\Delta B\ne0}&\propto \frac{E^2}{M_X^2},\\
\Gamma_p&\sim \frac{m_p^5}{M_X^4}.
\end{aligned}$ The decay-rate estimate has the usual dimension-six scaling, up to couplings and channel-dependent factors. A very large $M_X$ can make a cold proton effectively permanent while allowing baryon-changing reactions in a sufficiently energetic early plasma.

These are observational arguments within the lecture’s historical context, not claims about regions beyond our horizon.

p.src: Annihilation Leaves the Excess Behind

u.src: Annihilation Leaves the Excess Behind
en: Annihilation Leaves the Excess Behind
ja: 消滅は過剰を残す
zh: 湮灭留下过剩

p.src:
At high temperature, pair creation and annihilation run in both directions, $\gamma+\gamma\longleftrightarrow p+\bar p,
\qquad
E_{\gamma\gamma}\gtrsim2m_pc^2\approx2\,\mathrm{GeV}.$ As the bath cools, photons energetic enough to create a baryon pair become exponentially rare. Annihilation remains energetically allowed, but inverse production can no longer maintain equilibrium. Almost every proton finds an antiproton, and the small excess in equation [eq:c08-baryon-asymmetry] is what remains. The energetic annihilation photons quickly share their energy with the thermal bath.

ja.text: 高温では、対生成と対消滅は両方向に進む。
浴が冷えるにつれ、バリオン対を生成するのに十分なエネルギーを持つ光子は指数関数的に希少になる。消滅はエネルギー的に許されたままだが、逆生成はもはや平衡を維持できない。ほとんどすべての陽子は反陽子と出会い、式
[eq:c08-baryon-asymmetry]
の小さな過剰が残る。高エネルギーの消滅光子はすぐにそのエネルギーを熱浴と分かち合う。

zh.text: 在高温下，粒子对的产生与湮灭双向进行，
随着热浴冷却，能量足以产生重子对的光子变得指数级稀少。湮灭在能量上仍然允许，但逆产生过程已无法维持平衡。几乎每个质子都会找到一个反质子，而方程
[eq:c08-baryon-asymmetry]
中的微小过剩就是剩下的东西。高能湮灭光子迅速将其能量与热浴分享。

p.src: Equation [eq:c08-hubble-friction] makes the analogy precise. It has the same form as viscous motion, with drag coefficient $\gamma_{\rm cosmic}=3H.$ Expansion therefore slows the evolution of a homogeneous scalar field.
